name: Generic AML: Neo4j vs FalkorDB
notes: Public demo pack on a generic AML model. The private migration kit runs the same pack structure on your organisation's exact model and, inside your network, on your real data.

roles.name: AML Investigator
roles.summary: Works one customer or alert at a time: 360° view, triage, who else shares this customer's identifiers.

roles.name: Fraud Analyst
roles.summary: Hunts networks: shared counterparties, mule accounts, rings of customers sharing identifiers, paths between suspects.

roles.name: Compliance Officer / MLRO
roles.summary: Portfolio oversight: SAR and case pipeline, high-risk customers with open alerts, cash-intensive exposure, PEPs.

roles.name: Data Scientist (GDS)
roles.summary: Graph algorithms used in AML/fraud: components, centrality, communities, similarity.

roles.name: Engineering: semantic checks
roles.summary: Queries that expose behaviour differences between the engines on YOUR data, before anyone trusts a number.

queries.title: Customer 360
queries.what: Every relationship from one customer, grouped by type.
queries.cypher: MATCH (c:Customer {id: $cid})-[r]->(x) RETURN type(r) AS rel, count(x) AS n ORDER BY rel

queries.title: Alert triage
queries.what: From an alert to its customer, accounts, counterparties and total exposure.
queries.cypher: MATCH (al:Alert {id: $aid})<-[:HAS_ALERT]-(c:Customer)-[:OWNS]->(a:Account) OPTIONAL MATCH (a)-[t:TRANSACTED_WITH]->(ep:Counterparty) RETURN c.id AS customer, count(DISTINCT a) AS accounts, count(DISTINCT ep) AS counterparties, round(sum(t.totalAmount)) AS exposure ORDER BY customer

queries.title: Entity resolution
queries.what: Other customers sharing a phone, e-mail, tax ID or address with this customer.
queries.cypher: MATCH (c:Customer {id: $cid})-[:HAS_PHONE|HAS_EMAIL|HAS_TAX_ID|LIVES_AT]->(i)<-[:HAS_PHONE|HAS_EMAIL|HAS_TAX_ID|LIVES_AT]-(o:Customer) WHERE o <> c RETURN o.id AS other, count(DISTINCT i) AS shared ORDER BY shared DESC, other LIMIT 25

queries.title: Shared counterparties (4 hops)
queries.what: Customers whose accounts transact with the same counterparties as this customer's accounts.
queries.cypher: MATCH (c:Customer {id: $cid})-[:OWNS]->(:Account)-[:TRANSACTED_WITH]->(ep:Counterparty)<-[:TRANSACTED_WITH]-(:Account)<-[:OWNS]-(o:Customer) WHERE o <> c RETURN o.id AS other, count(DISTINCT ep) AS sharedCounterparties ORDER BY sharedCounterparties DESC, other LIMIT 20

queries.title: Mule-account candidates
queries.what: Accounts transacting with an unusually high number of counterparties (scan + aggregation over every transaction link).
queries.cypher: MATCH (a:Account)-[:TRANSACTED_WITH]->(ep:Counterparty) WITH a, count(ep) AS d WHERE d >= $min_degree RETURN a.id AS account, d ORDER BY d DESC, account LIMIT 20

queries.title: Identity rings (Cypher)
queries.what: Pairs of customers sharing two or more identifiers (phone, e-mail, address): the planted fraud rings.
queries.cypher: MATCH (c1:Customer)-[:HAS_PHONE|HAS_EMAIL|LIVES_AT]->(i)<-[:HAS_PHONE|HAS_EMAIL|LIVES_AT]-(c2:Customer) WHERE c1.id < c2.id WITH c1, c2, count(DISTINCT i) AS shared WHERE shared >= 2 RETURN count(*) AS suspiciousPairs

queries.title: Path between two suspects
queries.what: Shortest connection (up to 6 hops) between two customers.
queries.cypher_neo4j: MATCH (a:Customer {id: $cid}), (b:Customer {id: $cid2}) MATCH p = shortestPath((a)-[*..6]-(b)) RETURN length(p) AS hops
queries.cypher_falkordb: MATCH (a:Customer {id: $cid}), (b:Customer {id: $cid2}) WITH b, [a] AS f, CASE WHEN a = b THEN 0 END AS hops UNWIND CASE WHEN hops IS NULL THEN f ELSE [null] END AS x OPTIONAL MATCH (x)--(y) WITH b, hops, collect(DISTINCT y) AS f WITH b, f, coalesce(hops, CASE WHEN b IN f THEN 1 END) AS hops UNWIND CASE WHEN hops IS NULL THEN f ELSE [null] END AS x OPTIONAL MATCH (x)--(y) WITH b, hops, collect(DISTINCT y) AS f WITH b, f, coalesce(hops, CASE WHEN b IN f THEN 2 END) AS hops UNWIND CASE WHEN hops IS NULL THEN f ELSE [null] END AS x OPTIONAL MATCH (x)--(y) WITH b, hops, collect(DISTINCT y) AS f WITH b, f, coalesce(hops, CASE WHEN b IN f THEN 3 END) AS hops UNWIND CASE WHEN hops IS NULL THEN f ELSE [null] END AS x OPTIONAL MATCH (x)--(y) WITH b, hops, collect(DISTINCT y) AS f WITH b, f, coalesce(hops, CASE WHEN b IN f THEN 4 END) AS hops UNWIND CASE WHEN hops IS NULL THEN f ELSE [null] END AS x OPTIONAL MATCH (x)--(y) WITH b, hops, collect(DISTINCT y) AS f WITH b, f, coalesce(hops, CASE WHEN b IN f THEN 5 END) AS hops UNWIND CASE WHEN hops IS NULL THEN f ELSE [null] END AS x OPTIONAL MATCH (x)--(y) WITH b, hops, collect(DISTINCT y) AS f WITH b, f, coalesce(hops, CASE WHEN b IN f THEN 6 END) AS hops RETURN hops
queries.syntax_note: Neo4j uses its built-in shortestPath. The embedded FalkorDB build in this Space (4.18) has no undirected shortestPath and its algo.SPpaths enumerates paths (exponential at 6 hops), so FalkorDB runs the same search as a level-by-level breadth-first expansion in plain Cypher. Same answer; the FalkorDB server image in the migration kit also accepts RETURN length(shortestPath((a)-[*..6]-(b))).

queries.title: SAR and case pipeline
queries.what: Customers with SARs, number of SARs, and open cases.
queries.cypher: MATCH (c:Customer)-[:HAS_SAR]->(s:SAR) WITH count(DISTINCT c) AS sarCustomers, count(s) AS sars MATCH (k:Case) RETURN sarCustomers, sars, count(k) AS cases

queries.title: High-risk customers with open alerts, by branch
queries.what: Top branches by open alerts on High-risk customers.
queries.cypher: MATCH (b:Branch)<-[:BANKS_AT]-(c:Customer)-[:HAS_RISK_RATING]->(:RiskRating {band: 'High'}) MATCH (c)-[:HAS_ALERT]->(a:Alert {status: 'open'}) RETURN b.id AS branch, count(DISTINCT c) AS customers, count(a) AS openAlerts ORDER BY openAlerts DESC, branch LIMIT 10

queries.title: Cash-intensive exposure
queries.what: Customers in cash-intensive Industry sectors and their cash reports.
queries.cypher: MATCH (:Industry {sector: 'cash-intensive'})<-[:IN_INDUSTRY]-(c:Customer)-[:FILED_CASH_REPORT]->(l:CashReport) RETURN count(DISTINCT c) AS customers, count(l) AS cashReports, round(sum(l.amount)) AS total

queries.title: PEPs with alerts
queries.what: Politically exposed persons and their alerts.
queries.cypher: MATCH (c:Customer {pep: true})-[:HAS_ALERT]->(a:Alert) RETURN count(DISTINCT c) AS peps, count(a) AS alerts

queries.title: Connected components (WCC) on the identity network
queries.what: Weakly connected components over customers and shared phones, addresses, e-mails.
queries.cypher_falkordb: CALL algo.WCC({nodeLabels: ['Customer', 'Phone', 'Address', 'Email'], relationshipTypes: ['HAS_PHONE', 'LIVES_AT', 'HAS_EMAIL']}) YIELD node, componentId WITH componentId, count(*) AS size RETURN count(*) AS components, max(size) AS largest
queries.cypher_neo4j: CALL gds.wcc.stream('cmp_idn') YIELD nodeId, componentId WITH componentId, count(*) AS size RETURN count(*) AS components, max(size) AS largest
queries.neo4j_teardown: CALL gds.graph.drop('cmp_idn', false) YIELD graphName RETURN graphName
queries.syntax_note: Neo4j GDS works on an in-memory projection that must be built first (timed separately as 'projection'); FalkorDB runs the algorithm on the live graph.

queries.title: Degree centrality: busiest counterparties
queries.what: Counterparties with the most incoming transaction links (pure Cypher on both).
queries.cypher: MATCH (ep:Counterparty)<-[:TRANSACTED_WITH]-() WITH ep, count(*) AS degree RETURN ep.id AS party, degree ORDER BY degree DESC, party LIMIT 10

queries.title: PageRank on the transaction network
queries.what: Top 10 counterparties by PageRank over TRANSACTED_WITH.
queries.cypher_falkordb: CALL algo.pageRank(NULL, 'TRANSACTED_WITH') YIELD node, score RETURN node.id AS party ORDER BY score DESC, party LIMIT 10
queries.cypher_neo4j: CALL gds.pageRank.stream('cmp_tx') YIELD nodeId, score RETURN gds.util.asNode(nodeId).id AS party ORDER BY score DESC, party LIMIT 10
queries.neo4j_teardown: CALL gds.graph.drop('cmp_tx', false) YIELD graphName RETURN graphName
queries.syntax_note: Implementations differ in defaults (iterations, tolerance); compared by overlap of the top 10, not exact scores.

queries.title: Community detection (label propagation)
queries.what: Communities on the identity network with label propagation, available in both engines.
queries.cypher_falkordb: CALL algo.labelPropagation({nodeLabels: ['Customer', 'Phone', 'Address', 'Email'], relationshipTypes: ['HAS_PHONE', 'LIVES_AT', 'HAS_EMAIL']}) YIELD node, communityId RETURN count(DISTINCT communityId) AS communities
queries.cypher_neo4j: CALL gds.labelPropagation.stream('cmp_lpa') YIELD communityId RETURN count(DISTINCT communityId) AS communities
queries.neo4j_teardown: CALL gds.graph.drop('cmp_lpa', false) YIELD graphName RETURN graphName
queries.syntax_note: Label propagation implementations differ (iteration limits, tie-breaking, direction handling), so community counts are not expected to match; shown for timing and as a capability that exists in both.

queries.title: Louvain / Leiden communities
queries.what: Modularity-based community detection used for fraud-ring detection.
queries.cypher_neo4j: CALL gds.louvain.stream('cmp_lv') YIELD communityId RETURN count(DISTINCT communityId) AS communities
queries.neo4j_teardown: CALL gds.graph.drop('cmp_lv', false) YIELD graphName RETURN graphName
queries.cypher_falkordb: MATCH (c:Customer)-[:HAS_PHONE|LIVES_AT|HAS_EMAIL]->(x) RETURN id(c) AS a, id(x) AS b UNION ALL MATCH (n:Customer) RETURN -1 AS a, count(n) AS b UNION ALL MATCH (n:Phone) RETURN -1 AS a, count(n) AS b UNION ALL MATCH (n:Address) RETURN -1 AS a, count(n) AS b UNION ALL MATCH (n:Email) RETURN -1 AS a, count(n) AS b
queries.syntax_note: FalkorDB has no in-database Louvain/Leiden. Workaround timed here: one Cypher query exports the same identity subgraph, then Louvain runs outside the database (python-igraph, community_multilevel). FalkorDB time = export + Louvain. Community counts differ slightly by implementation; label propagation (D4) is the in-database alternative.

queries.title: Node similarity: counterparty similarity
queries.what: Accounts with the most similar sets of counterparties (Jaccard).
queries.cypher_neo4j: CALL gds.nodeSimilarity.stream('cmp_sim', {topK: 1, degreeCutoff: 25}) YIELD similarity RETURN count(*) AS pairs, round(avg(similarity) * 1000) / 1000 AS avgSimilarity
queries.neo4j_teardown: CALL gds.graph.drop('cmp_sim', false) YIELD graphName RETURN graphName
queries.cypher_falkordb: MATCH (a:Account)-[:TRANSACTED_WITH]->(c:Counterparty) WITH a, collect(DISTINCT id(c)) AS cs WHERE size(cs) >= 25 RETURN id(a) AS account, cs AS counterparties
queries.syntax_note: FalkorDB has no in-database node-similarity procedure. Workaround timed here: one Cypher query exports each account's counterparties (degree cutoff 25 applied in the database), then the same Jaccard top-1 calculation as gds.nodeSimilarity runs outside the database in Python. FalkorDB time = export + similarity. Embeddings (FastRP, Node2Vec, GraphSAGE) remain Neo4j-GDS-only.

queries.title: Parallel relationships
queries.what: Counts transaction links two ways. If the data has parallel relationships (same account and counterparty twice), FalkorDB's count(ep) counts distinct neighbours while Neo4j counts every relationship.
queries.cypher: MATCH (a:Account)-[t:TRANSACTED_WITH]->(ep:Counterparty) WITH count(t) AS relationships MATCH (a:Account)-[:TRANSACTED_WITH]->(ep:Counterparty) WITH relationships, a, count(ep) AS d RETURN relationships, sum(d) AS countedViaNeighbours
queries.syntax_note: On data without parallel relationships both columns are equal on both engines. On FalkorDB with parallel relationships the second column is lower: bind the relationship variable in counting queries.
